Einkorn & Spelt Cinnamon Rolls |
Baking Great Bread
by  Henry Hunter Jr.  • recipepantry.app
PREP TIME
1 hour
RISE TIME
2 hours 5 minutes
(first rise plus final
proof)
BAKE TIME
24 to 28 minutes
YIELD
Twelve rolls in a
9x13 inch pan
(about 77g of
dough each, before
frosting)
Soft, tender, and wholly whole grain.
Ingredients
Tangzhong
36g  fresh-milled spelt flour
180g  whole milk

Dough
300g  fresh-milled spelt flour
144g  fresh-milled einkorn flour
90g  whole milk, lukewarm
1 large egg (50g)  room temperature
50g  cane sugar
60g  unsalted butter, softened
6g  fine sea salt
7g  instant yeast
Cinnamon Filling
56g  unsalted butter, very soft
130g  dark brown sugar, packed
14g  ground cinnamon
1g  ground cardamom
1g  fine sea salt
Maple Cream Cheese Frosting
115g  cream cheese, softened
28g  unsalted butter, softened
40g  pure maple syrup
60g  powdered sugar
4g  vanilla extract
1g  fine sea salt
Pan
10g  unsalted butter, for the pan
Equipment
•  Grain mill
•  Kitchen scale
•  Stand mixer with dough hook
•  Small saucepan and whisk
•  9x13 inch metal baking pan
•  Rolling pin
•  Unflavored dental floss or serrated knife
•  Instant-read thermometer

Instructions
1 .  Mill the Flour
Mill both grains fresh and let them cool.
1 .  Mill and cool
Mill about 345g spelt berries and 150g einkorn berries on a medium-fine setting. Spread the
flour in a wide bowl and let it cool for 10 to 15 minutes. Weigh out what you need.
36g  fresh-milled spelt flour  300g  fresh-milled spelt flour  144g  fresh-milled einkorn flour
💡  Einkorn flour is yellow and soft. Spelt is fluffy and pale. Weigh both.
2 .  Make the Tangzhong
Cook a little flour and milk into a pudding. It holds water, and that keeps the rolls soft for days.
1 .  Cook the paste
Whisk the spelt flour and milk together in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Keep
whisking for 3 to 4 minutes, until it thickens like pudding and the whisk leaves lines. That's a
tangzhong, and it should read about 149°F (65°C).
36g  fresh-milled spelt flour  180g  whole milk
2 .  Cool the paste
Scrape it into a bowl, press plastic wrap against the surface, and cool for 15 minutes until
lukewarm.
10/15/26, 8:20 AM  Einkorn & Spelt Cinnamon Rolls | Baking Great Bread - Print Version | Recipe Pantry
https://recipepantry.app/recipes/einkorn-spelt-maple-cinnamon-rolls/print  3/8

3 .  Mix and Knead
Mix, rest, then knead in the butter.
1 .  Mix and rest
In your mixer bowl, combine the tangzhong, milk, egg, sugar, and yeast. Add the spelt flour,
einkorn flour, and salt. Mix on low for 2 minutes until no dry flour is left, then cover and rest for
20 minutes.
90g  whole milk, lukewarm  1 large egg (50g)  room temperature  50g  cane sugar
7g  instant yeast  300g  fresh-milled spelt flour  144g  fresh-milled einkorn flour
6g  fine sea salt
2 .  Knead in the butter
With the mixer on medium-low, add the soft butter in three pieces, letting each disappear before
the next. Knead 8 to 10 minutes total, until the dough is smooth, soft, and tacky. A small piece
should stretch into a thin windowpane, though it may tear sooner than a white-flour dough
would. Einkorn gluten is weak and stretchy, so stop when it's smooth and don't add extra flour.
60g  unsalted butter, softened
💡  This is a soft enriched dough. If it feels sticky, wait. The flour is still drinking.
4 .  First Rise
Let the dough puff up until it looks airy and jiggly.
1 .  Ferment
Move the dough to a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let it rise at 76 to 78°F (24 to 26°C) for 60 to
90 minutes. The bulk fermentation is done when the dough is about 50 percent bigger, puffy,
and jiggles when you shake the bowl.
10/15/26, 8:20 AM  Einkorn & Spelt Cinnamon Rolls | Baking Great Bread - Print Version | Recipe Pantry
https://recipepantry.app/recipes/einkorn-spelt-maple-cinnamon-rolls/print  4/8

5 .  Fill and Roll
A paste filling stays put and keeps the swirl tight.
1 .  Make the filling
Mash the very soft butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt together with a fork until
it's a spreadable paste.
56g  unsalted butter, very soft  130g  dark brown sugar, packed  14g  ground cinnamon
1g  ground cardamom  1g  fine sea salt
2 .  Roll out the dough
Grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) metal pan with the pan butter. Turn the dough onto a lightly
floured counter and roll it into a rectangle about 12 x 18 inches (30 x 46 cm), long side facing
you.
10g  unsalted butter, for the pan
3 .  Spread and roll
Spread the filling over the dough, leaving a 1/2 inch (1.3 cm) bare border along the far long
edge. Roll up tightly from the long edge toward the border and pinch the seam closed.
4 .  Cut and pan
Cut the log into 12 equal rolls with unflavored dental floss or a sharp serrated knife. Set them
cut side up in the pan, 3 rows of 4.
💡  Make-ahead option: cover the pan tightly after cutting and refrigerate 8 to 14 hours. Next day, set it out for
45 to 60 minutes before baking.
6 .  Final Proof
Let the rolls puff until they touch.
1 .  Proof the rolls
Cover the pan and let the rolls proof for 45 to 60 minutes, until they look puffy, touch each other,
and a floured fingertip leaves a dimple that fills back slowly. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C)
during the last 20 minutes.
10/15/26, 8:20 AM  Einkorn & Spelt Cinnamon Rolls | Baking Great Bread - Print Version | Recipe Pantry
https://recipepantry.app/recipes/einkorn-spelt-maple-cinnamon-rolls/print  5/8

7 .  Bake the Rolls
Pull them when they're golden and cooked through.
1 .  Bake
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 24 to 28 minutes, until the tops are golden and the center roll reads
190°F (88°C). Tent loosely with foil after 15 minutes if the tops brown fast.
2 .  Cool briefly
Cool the pan on a rack for 10 minutes. You want the rolls warm, not hot, when the frosting goes
on.
8 .  Frost and Serve
Warm rolls melt the frosting into every crack.
1 .  Make the frosting
Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth. Beat in the maple syrup, powdered sugar,
vanilla, and salt until creamy.
115g  cream cheese, softened  28g  unsalted butter, softened  40g  pure maple syrup
60g  powdered sugar  4g  vanilla extract  1g  fine sea salt
2 .  Frost
Spread the frosting over the warm rolls and serve right away.
💡  Too warm and the frosting runs off. Too cool and it sits on top. Warm to the touch is right.

Roll and Cut
Classic Roll-and-Cut
1 .  Roll
Roll the dough into a 12 x 18 inch rectangle, spread the filling, and roll tightly from the long
edge.
2 .  Cut
Cut into 12 rolls and place in the pan, 3 rows of 4.
Overnight Make-Ahead
1 .  Chill
After cutting and panning, cover tightly and refrigerate 8 to 14 hours.
2 .  Warm up
Set the pan out for 45 to 60 minutes, until the rolls look puffy, then bake as written.
Bake the Rolls
Temperature:  350 °F /  175 °C
IF USING:  METAL 9X13 PAN (RECOMMENDED)
1 .  Bake
Bake 24 to 28 minutes at 350°F (175°C), tenting with foil after 15 minutes if needed.
IF USING:  GLASS BAKING DISH
1 .  Bake
Lower the oven to 325°F (165°C) and bake 28 to 32 minutes.

Storage
Room Temperature:  Unfrosted rolls keep 2 days covered. Frosted rolls should sit out no
more than 2 hours.
Refrigerated:  Frosted, up to 5 days, covered
Frozen:  Unfrosted, up to 3 months, wrapped individually
Refresh:  Warm a refrigerated roll for 15 to 20 seconds in the microwave. Thaw frozen rolls
overnight, warm at 300°F (150°C) for 10 minutes, then frost.
💡  Freeze the rolls unfrosted and make a fresh batch of frosting when you serve them.
FAQ
Why use a tangzhong in a whole grain roll?
Whole grain flour is thirsty and can bake up dry. The cooked paste locks in water, so the rolls stay
soft and tender for days.
Can I use store-bought whole grain flour instead of milling?
Yes. Use the same weights of whole grain spelt and einkorn flour. Hold back 10g of the milk and
add it only if the dough feels stiff after the rest.
My rolls came out dense. What went wrong?
Usually too much flour added during rolling, or an under-proofed pan. Roll on a barely floured
counter and wait until the rolls touch before baking.
Can I make these with all einkorn?
Not with this formula. Einkorn alone needs less liquid and a gentler knead. Keeping it at 30
percent gives you softness and a reliable rise.
Can I make them dairy-free?
Swap in unsweetened oat milk and plant butter, and use a plant-based cream cheese for the
frosting. The rolls will be a little less rich.
